LESSON: TRANS SAHARAN SLAVE TRADE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.3: Trans Saharan Slave Trade

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Trans Saharan Slave Trade. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do people subject others to slave trade?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa
2. describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa
3. demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TRANS SAHARAN SLAVE TRADE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Trans Saharan Slave Trade helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: TRANS SAHARAN SLAVE TRADE
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Trans Saharan Slave Trade” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Trans Saharan Slave Trade.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Trans Saharan Slave Trade is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Trans Saharan Slave Trade” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Trans Saharan Slave Trade. (skill: describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Trans Saharan Slave Trade to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa.
3. Practise this skill: describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.
4. Practise this skill: demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Trans Saharan Slave Trade from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Trans Saharan Slave Trade: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Trans Saharan Slave Trade?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do people subject others to slave trade?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Trans Saharan Slave Trade means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify factors that led to development of Trans- Saharan slave Trade in Africa.
5. Be able to: describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
